transcript.user_1_turn_1: A few friends are coming over after pizza tonight. There'll be five of us, and Sam has played maybe two board games in his life.
transcript.user_2_turn_1: That sounds like a night for something you can teach without turning the table into a rules seminar. What games are actually in the running?
transcript.user_1_turn_2: I know Mosslight Market pretty well. It plays three to five, takes around 35 to 45 minutes, and everyone's running the same little market together.
transcript.user_2_turn_2: That already checks a lot of boxes for a mixed group.
transcript.user_1_turn_3: Priya brought Clockwork Crows too. It looks amazing, but none of us has opened it. The box says two to four players and about an hour to seventy-five minutes.
transcript.user_2_turn_3: Pretty box, slightly awkward timing. With five people you'd either be leaving someone out or splitting the group before you've even learned it.
transcript.user_1_turn_4: Yeah, and Jo kind of disappears when a game gets really competitive or has lots of take-that stuff. Priya loves that kind of thing, though.
transcript.user_2_turn_4: Then Clockwork sounds more like a future Priya night than an everyone-at-the-table night.
transcript.user_1_turn_5: Pizza should show up around 7:30, and Sam has to catch the 9:15 bus, so we're not going to have this huge block of time.
transcript.user_2_turn_5: Right, once you eat and clear the table, an hour-long first play could get tight fast.
transcript.user_1_turn_6: I mostly want one game where all five of us are laughing together and nobody's checking the clock or apologizing for not understanding the rules.
